task: Find and implement user-facing improvements for the installable multi-CLI desktop app.

expected_items.description: Use current external references and existing local architecture before deciding what to add.
Give users direct setup and verification guidance for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, and OpenCode without making one CLI mandatory.
Let users start CLI lanes with simple reusable modes instead of writing every prompt from scratch.
Let the desktop app list deferred human decisions and record user answers so paused CLI lanes can be resumed later.
Do not auto-install external CLIs or make global environment changes as part of this user improvement slice.
expected_items.source: CLI adapter policy and installation audit rules

expected_items.description: Ship a signed, notarized, auto-updating public macOS installer.
expected_items.rationale: This slice improves the current desktop runtime and user controls. Public macOS readiness requires Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, notarization, update, rollback, and privacy/dependency review.

artifact_checks.purpose: Tauri commands for CLI sessions, scoped editing, and human decision inbox list/answer.
Desktop UI for setup guidance, mode presets, session controls, and decision answers.
Responsive styling for the new Desktop controls.
Implementation contract for the desktop orchestration slice.
Trace request to outcome and verification.

acceptance_checks.description: Type and lint check the monitor UI after adding setup, mode, and decision inbox controls.
Run monitor tests and static build so generated snapshot/out artifacts include the new records.
Run platform desktop tests and readiness scan for the added command/UI strings.
Compile the Tauri app with Rust/Cargo.
acceptance_checks.rationale: Rust/Cargo is not installed in this environment, so direct Tauri compile verification is unavailable.

known_omission_risks: Actual CLI authentication and installation flows are still manual guidance, not an in-app setup wizard.
The decision inbox answer is recorded in JSON, but automatic lane resume is still a future workflow.
PTY terminal behavior and Monaco-level editor integration remain future implementation slices.
notes: This slice intentionally improves user controls without performing global installation or requiring any one CLI.
